To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose and evaluate a new task-oriented search framework that leverages procedural knowledge, and that we demonstrate the utility of our framework by showing improvements in search quality over a variety of baselines and commercial search engines.

we propose to create a new three-way parallel corpus for task-oriented search, and develop a set of textual and structural features to automatically identify key search phrases and extract wikiHow-style knowledge from search queries, and that our proposed approach outperforms baseline algorithms and the (manuslly-curated) wikihow knowledge base.

we propose a set of features for task-oriented search and automatic procedural knowledge base construction, and we demonstrate that our proposed approach improves search results for task-oriented search.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: Can procedural knowledge be extracted from search queries and query contexts?
the development of a task-oriented search engine that leverages existing procedural knowledge to suggest relevant tasks, and to automatically extract procedural knowledge from users' search logs.
the development of a new task-oriented search engine that leverages procedural knowledge, which is a first step in the development of a task-oriented search assistant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed approach has a promising potential to improve search quality for task-oriented search, but further research is needed to improve the performance of our approach.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using procedural knowledge bases to improve task-oriented search, and that our proposed approach is promising.
we have shown that it is possible to automatically construct a procedural knowledge base for task-oriented search from user search logs and task descriptions, with a high level of accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) we show the feasibility of using task-oriented search to improve procedural knowledge construction and vice versa; (2) our approach is able to improve task-oriented search results by 10% over the best performing commercial search engines; (3) we propose a novel set of textual and structural features for task-oriented search and procedural knowledge extraction.

task-oriented search can leverage procedural knowledge for task suggestion and search query understanding, while automatic procedural knowledge base construction can leverage users' search activities.
task-oriented search and procedural knowledge base construction can benefit from each other, and that the combination of both can improve task-oriented search quality and experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
procedural knowledge can be used to enhance task-oriented search, and that automatic procedural knowledge base construction from search logs can benefit from the use of search task suggestion.
procedural knowledge can be extracted from user queries and query contexts and used to enhance task-oriented search.

task-oriented search and procedural knowledge construction are complementary to each other: the former can benefit from the latter and the latter can benefit from the former, and that both problems can be solved by leveraging the other.
